text:
PagerBot: 🚨 ALERT: CDN POP connectivity degradation detected in eu-west-1 (POP-ams-03). Packet loss > 12% for last 5m, increased 5xx rates observed for streaming and embeddings routes. Pager: @oncall-sre.

Alex L.: seeing it on our dashboards too — p50 tail latency spiking on /v1/embeddings for eu traffic. Any idea whether this is last-mile or upstream CDN fabric?

Maria G.: running quick checks: mtr to pop edge shows heavy loss after the POP's egress hop. paste:```mtr -r -c 10 pop-ams-03.cdn.example
Start: 2025-10-12 14:07:01
HOST: runner            Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1. 10.0.0.1              0.0%    10    0.2   0.5   0.1   1.1   0.3
 2. 100.64.12.5           0.0%    10    1.1   1.3   1.0   2.2   0.3
 3. 193.0.14.7           12.0%    10   10.4  11.0   9.8  15.2   1.6
 4. pop-ams-03.cdn.example 12.0%   10   10.6  11.2  10.0  15.5   1.7
```

Cheng W.: that looks like packet loss at or just before the POP egress, likely a provider edge/regional backbone flapping. Any BGP churn alerts from the CDN provider?

NetOps Bot: CDN provider (EdgeZone) event: "partial egress disruption in ams region" — incident ID EZ-2025-AMS-87, started 2025-10-12T13:58:12Z. Provider notes increased queue drops on pop-ams-03.

Oncall SRE: I'm on it. Triage plan: 1) confirm customer impact and scope; 2) attempt regional routing failover to alternate POP (pop-ams-02) for critical routes; 3) open provider ticket with EZ; 4) notify CS for customer comms. Alex/Maria — are you able to test failover config?

Alex L.: yes, I can push a targeted route policy for embeddings and streaming: set edge-preference for eu-west to pop-ams-02 with lower cost. Will test on 0.5% of traffic first. Command:```curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routing/edge-preference -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","from_pop":"pop-ams-03","to_pop":"pop-ams-02","weight":0.995}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN'```

Maria G.: starting a small canary now. Monitoring logs. If anyone needs to revert:```curl -X DELETE https://console.internal/api/v1/routing/edge-preference?region=eu-west-1```

Olivia (CS): Can we get a quick impact assessment for customers in EU? Which tenants are routed via pop-ams-03 by default? I need a short blurb for status page.

Alex L.: pulling tenant routing map... most EU tenants use pop-ams-03 as primary; critical customers A, B, C have multi-pop fallback enabled. Early telemetry: canary (0.5%) shows error rate dropped back to baseline for that subset.

Oncall SRE: good. Maria — if canary stays stable for 60s, increase to 20%. Watch for cache miss storms.

Maria G.: canary stable at 60s, ramping to 20%. Watch: slight increase in origin traffic due to cache warm-up, but 5xx rate trending down.

Cheng W.: keep an eye on BGP table. If provider is flapping, re-routing may create asymmetric paths. Recommend enabling connection tracking bailouts per runbook EX-EDGE-6:```edgectl connection-bailout --region eu-west-1 --threshold 10% --dry-run=false```

PagerBot: Note: automatic customer-facing status update prepared draft.

Olivia (CS): Draft OK — short blurb: "We are investigating degraded connectivity affecting customers in EU (eu-west-1). Some customers may experience increased latency and request errors. We are mitigating by shifting traffic to alternate POPs; updates to follow." I'll post once we have confirmed broader failover.

NetOps Bot: Provider updated: "EZ-2025-AMS-87: mitigation in progress; we are draining affected egress interfaces and provisioning spare capacity. Estimated time to stabilize 15-45 minutes."

Oncall SRE: pushing to 100% fallback for critical routes now. Command:```curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routing/edge-preference -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","to_pop":"pop-ams-02","weight":1.0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN'```

Alex L.: applied. Rolling restart of edge proxies for eu-west to pick up new routing; staging concurrency limit to avoid origin storms. Logs show connection drain proceeding.

Maria G.: monitoring shows packet loss at pop-ams-03 dropping to near zero at 14:15:xx as provider drains the interface. Application error rates returning to baseline across EU.

Olivia (CS): posting status update now to customers, linking to incident ID EZ-2025-AMS-87 and our mitigation steps. Message: "We have shifted traffic to an alternate POP and are monitoring. Some latency may persist as caches warm. We'll update when EZ confirms full restoration."

Oncall SRE: handoff at 14:20 UTC — Cheng, you're taking second-shift for watch. Note: keep the provider ticket open and request RCA and timeline for long-term mitigations. I'll update the incident timeline and start an evergreen postmortem doc.

Cheng W.: taking over. Will keep monitoring BGP and edge metrics. Also schedule a quick follow-up with EdgeZone for a technical review of why egress queue drops occurred.

PagerBot: Incident severity set to Sev2. Tags: cdn, edge, eu-west-1, provider-incident, mitigation-failover.

Oncall SRE: quick action items to capture in postmortem: - why automatic cross-pop load balancing didn't absorb the hit; - whether our fallback weight defaults are aggressive enough; - evaluate automated warm-warm cache prefill during edge failover.

Alex L.: note to infra: add an observability alert for sudden spike in origin RPS following edge-pop failover (to detect cache-storms early).

Maria G.: leaving logs/pcap snippets in the incident doc: `s3://incidents/2025-10-12/1771000000/pcap-ams-03.zip` — useful for provider deep-dive.

Olivia (CS): Customers A and B acknowledged the update and appreciate the proactive failover. No escalations for now.

Cheng W.: provider EZ closed their mitigation window at 14:40 UTC, marking the event as "stabilized"; we will keep traffic routed to pop-ams-02 for another hour to be safe, then re-evaluate.

Oncall SRE: thanks team. I'll add a follow-up to schedule postmortem sync and remediate runbook gaps. If anything regresses, page as usual. :thumbsup:

Alex L.: noted. Signing off from active mitigation.

PagerBot: Incident thread closed for active mitigation at 14:45 UTC; monitoring-only (oncall: Cheng W.).
